links.outcome: External validation performance across cohorts with distribution shifts versus internal validation
links.effect: Internal AUC 0.91-0.98; external AUC 0.75-0.95 across 5 external cohorts; performance worsened vs internal but differences not significant.
links.quote: While the performance of all models worsened compared with the internal test sets, the differences were not significant, as shown in Figure S11 in Multimedia Appendix 1 .

links.outcome: ML models compared against baseline biomarkers and prior ML models on same internal test data
links.effect: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed MDW, CRP, Sepsis Index, COMPOSER, and Mindray SVM baselines across all decision thresholds.
links.quote: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed all the baseline comparison methods (ie, MDW [ 37 ], CRP [ 44 ], Sepsis Index [ 45 ], COMPOSER [ 25 ], as well as the SVM model developed in the study by Aguirre and Urrechaga [ 31 ]; Figures 1 and 2 ; Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ) and did so across all possible decision thresholds.

links.outcome: Performance under dataset shift (covariate, label, missingness) between training and external cohorts
links.effect: Good generalization overall, but XGB had low sNB on UD-ED (most dissimilar to training set) and low PPV and sNB on OGSA-ICU (missing MDW, second most dissimilar).
links.quote: The XGB model achieved acceptable-to-excellent performance on all external datasets and with respect to all metrics, except for the sNB on the UD-ED: this dataset was, among the external validation datasets, the most dissimilar to the internal training set (PA-ED).

links.outcome: Model performance reported separately across five external sites/settings and analyzers
links.effect: Performance varied by site: acceptable-to-excellent on external cohorts, but low PPV and sNB in OGSA-ICU with a different analyzer and no MDW.
links.quote: The XGB-based system achieved low PPV and sNB on the OGSA-ICU dataset, as also shown in Figure S13 in Multimedia Appendix 1 , which was also the second most dissimilar to the internal training set (PA-ED).

links.outcome: Performance when a key input (MDW) was entirely missing, using imputation
links.effect: Lack of MDW (100% missing) led to a large decrease in PPV despite imputation, though overall performance was acceptable.
links.quote: While, indeed, the obtained results show that acceptable results could be obtained even in the presence of significant missingness shift, the lack of MDW led to a relevant drop in performance, thus highlighting the need for collecting complete data in practical scenarios.

links.outcome: Cautious classifiers (abstention when confidence uncertain) versus standard models on sensitivity, PPV, NPV
links.effect: For XGB, PDR, RF, LR (except OGSA-ICU), cautious classification improved both sensitivity and PPV with equal or better NPV; coverage >50% in all cases and >70% in all but 3.
links.quote: For XGB, PDR, RF, and LR (except for the OGSA-ICU dataset), cautious classification led to an improvement in both sensitivity and PPV and equivalent or better performance in terms of NPV.

unlisted_practices: Cautious classification (abstention below confidence threshold) to control error rates
Derivation of interpretable decision rules from decision trees with clinical experts
Imputation model for missing MDW input in settings lacking the biomarker

links.outcome: internal and external sepsis detection performance
links.effect: Internal AUC 0.91-0.98; external AUC 0.75-0.95 across validation datasets.
links.quote: The developed models achieved good performance on the internal validation (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve between 0.91 and 0.98), as well as consistent generalization performance across the external validation datasets (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve between 0.75 and 0.95), outperforming baseline biomarkers and state-of-the-art ML models for sepsis detection.

links.outcome: robustness to missingness and distribution shifts
links.effect: External validation was generally acceptable, but missing MDW caused a relevant performance drop, especially PPV.
links.quote: While, indeed, the obtained results show that acceptable results could be obtained even in the presence of significant missingness shift, the lack of MDW led to a relevant drop in performance, thus highlighting the need for collecting complete data in practical scenarios.

links.outcome: candidate models versus biomarker and ML baselines
links.effect: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed MDW, CRP, Sepsis Index, COMPOSER, and Mindray SVM across all thresholds.
links.quote: XGB, RF, and LR significantly outperformed all the baseline comparison methods (ie, MDW [ 37 ], CRP [ 44 ], Sepsis Index [ 45 ], COMPOSER [ 25 ], as well as the SVM model developed in the study by Aguirre and Urrechaga [ 31 ]; Figures 1 and 2 ; Figure S1 in Multimedia Appendix 1 ) and did so across all possible decision thresholds.

screen.practice: cautious classification (abstention) and explainability for robustness to distribution shift
screen.reason: The study develops and externally validates a sepsis prediction model across multiple hospital datasets experiencing distribution shifts, specifically testing the safeguard practice of cautious classification (abstaining from uncertain predictions) to maintain reliability under distribution shift.
